Content baseline for the library, recorded in-session via evals/workflow-runner.mjs (Workflow tool, subscription) at k=1, option A (the GREEN generator may read files inside the skill's own directory; RED stays tool-less). 'model' is the resolved id the agents ran on; the runner's 'opus' pin is a harness shorthand and was substituted here. All runs executed on the 1M-context variant of claude-opus-5, recorded under the base id so they stay comparable with API-side runs.

COVERAGE, in three runs, staged by reference mass. 2026-08-15, branch main / parent 45aa919, run wf_225687a2-7f5: a 6-skill validation probe, 23 cases — the three most reference-heavy skills (architecture-design, performance-optimization, architecture-documentation) and three carrying no references at all (plan-execution, project-review, resilience-engineering). 2026-08-18, branch feat/reference-aware-evals / parent 69cf2d3: the 25 skills whose references+templates outweigh their SKILL.md, 86 cases. 2026-08-19, same branch / parent 35dc048: the 22 skills carrying some references but less than their SKILL.md, 86 cases. 53 of 66 skills, 195 cases. PARTIAL by design — uncovered cases simply do not gate; the 13 skills with no references at all are recorded in a later run.

Refresh by re-running the in-session runner, or `python evals/run.py --all --update-baseline` (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus EVAL_GEN_MODEL/EVAL_JUDGE_MODEL). The gate (run.py / skill-evals.yml) fails if an assertion green here later goes red on a same-model row; rows recorded on a different model are reported 'not comparable' and skipped rather than flagged. k=1 is noisy on some cases — accepted; majority voting in the Workflow arm is a tracked follow-up.

Rows knowingly recorded red must not be 'fixed' by editing this file — a recorded false can never fire the regression check, so keeping it is safe, and each one is an authoring lead. Nineteen assertions scored RED true / GREEN false, i.e. the skill made the model stop doing something it did without the skill: performance-optimization eval:2[0] ('asks to see the current query and database schema'), accessibility-design eval:3[7], api-design eval:1[4] and [5], compliance-privacy eval:2[2], dependency-impact-analysis eval:3[1], incident-response eval:1[1], ml-experiment-tracking eval:2[2], refactoring eval:1[1], release-management eval:2[4] and eval:3[3], strategic-review eval:1[0] and [4] and eval:2[4], test-data-strategy eval:1[7] and eval:3[6], test-suite-design eval:1[3] and eval:3[7], ui-ux-design eval:3[3]. Six of those cases score GREEN below RED overall (api-design eval:1 7→6, compliance-privacy eval:2 5→4, incident-response eval:1 6→5, release-management eval:3 4→3, strategic-review eval:1 2→1, ui-ux-design eval:3 5→4) and are worth a higher-k re-run before being treated as settled floors.
